Stack Trace

You might say

The terminal printed a long error. Which line should I send to the AI?

The position list printed when a program fails, ordered from the failure point back to the entry·In JavaScript and Node.js, a stack trace commonly lists the frame nearest the throw near the top, followed by its callers. Start near the top and find a frame in your own file; it gives a location clue, not proof of the root cause.
Know first
Terminal
Stack Trace
Click each frame to see which line of your code it points to
Terminal
$ node save.js
save.js:24
  return items.map((row) => row);
                 ^
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
save.jsLine 24
4function handleSave(request) {
5 const items = loadRows(request.file);
6 return items.map((row) => row.total);
7}
22function loadRows(file) {
23 const items = readFile(file);
24 return items.map((row) => row);
25}

This is your own file: items is undefined and line 24 calls .map on it. Start here.

A stack trace usually lists the frame nearest the throw first, followed by its callers. Start near the top and find a frame in your own file; frames locate clues but do not prove the root cause.

How to read a stack trace

The frame near the throw is usually near the top: The frame nearest the throw is usually near the top, followed by its callers; a runtime or third-party frame may appear first.

Look for your own files only: The trace can mix in runtime and third-party library internals. Only frames from your own files correspond to code you wrote and can be a starting point for a fix.

The error type points at a value: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined means code tried to read a property from undefined; check the failing line and actual data to find which value was undefined.

What it does not tell you

A stack trace says where it failed, not why. The same error can come from empty data, a wrong argument, or an upstream change, so the cause still needs code and real data to confirm.

You can say this to an AI Agent

“

Running node save.js reports a TypeError, and the stack points to my loadRows (save.js:24:21). Start near that frame, then trace its caller and input data to find where undefined first appears; rerun after the fix and verify the result.
